All 16 reference classes viewed. Now making my final analysis.

**Test image summary:**
- Stem shown horizontally with the crown/root junction on the right
- **Abundant fluffy white cottony mycelium** concentrated at the soil-line/crown area
- Roots visible with soil, stem itself shows some discoloration/bleaching
- Classic "crown rot" presentation

**Comparison results:**
- **Southern_Blight**: Best visual match — white mycelium fanning out at the soil line/crown area, consistent with *Sclerotium rolfsii* growth pattern
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Has white mycelium but reference showed large black sclerotia not visible in the test image
- **Gray_Mold**: Gray (not white) fluffy growth, mostly on fruit/stems above soil
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: Gray-brown mycelium primarily on fruit
- All bacterial wilt/leaf diseases: No white mycelium — eliminated

The white fluffy mycelium at the stem crown near the soil line is the hallmark of **Southern_Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*), and it matches the reference images for that class most closely.
